chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Mu'ammar ibn Khallad who said:

I asked Abu Al-Hassan (peace be upon him) about standing up for the rulers, so he (peace be upon him) said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: Dissimulation (Taqiyya) is from my religion and the religion of my forefathers, and there is no faith for the one who has no dissimulation.

key_terms.إِيمَانَ: Faith; deep belief and conviction, here linked directly to the practice of Taqiyya.
key_terms.التَّقِيَّة: Dissimulation; the practice of concealing one's beliefs or true self for protection in times of danger or oppression.
key_terms.الْقِيَامِ لِلْوُلَاةِ: Standing up for the rulers; showing respect or deference to political authorities.

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of Taqiyya in Shia theology according to Imam Al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated by Mu'amar ibn Khalad from Imam al-Rida (AS), explicitly links the practice of Taqiyya to the Prophet's family, establishing it as a fundamental pillar of Shia identity and survival. By stating that 'there is no faith for one who has no Taqiyya,' Imam al-Rida underscores that dissimulation is not merely a legal concession but an essential attribute of true belief, particularly crucial during periods of political oppression by rulers. This teaching reflects the historical reality of the Shia community navigating power dynamics while preserving their religious integrity.

en.hubeali: From him, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Moammar Bin Khallad who said,

‘I asked Abu Al-Hassanasws about the standing up to the ruler. So heasws said: ‘Abu Ja’farasws said: ‘The dissimulation (Taqiyya) is from myasws Religion and the Religion of myasws forefathersasws, and there is no Eman for the one who has no dissimulation (Taqiyya) for him’.
en.sarwar: 12. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Mu’ammar ibn Khallad who has said the following: “

Once I asked abu al-Hassan (a.s.) about standing up to salute the rulers (to show respect). He said that abu Ja’far (a.s.) has said, ‘Al-Taqiyyah is my religion and the religion of my predecessors. Whoever disregards al-Taqiyyah has no belief.”’
